intro: Picture this: you wake up, open the curtains to the Rayong River flowing past your room, sip coffee in a quiet riverside garden, then walk a few minutes to explore century-old wooden shophouses on Yommarat Road, the old quarter Rayong locals are proud of — Madina Hotel Rayong, or "Madina Rayong," is a riverside lifestyle hotel at 41 Rim Nam Road, Tha Pradu, in central Rayong · the name "Madina" comes from the Thai "ma-dee," meaning to bring in good things · open since 2008 and renovated in 2023, it has 72 rooms, many with river views, plus the Kesara restaurant, Two Hundreds Coffee café, gym-yoga, and free parking · rooms from about THB 700/night, scoring 8.2 from 40 reviews on Trip.com.

body.html: Madina Hotel Rayong — who it's for — the shortest possible summary: Madina Hotel Rayong is a mid-size riverside lifestyle hotel for people who want to stay in central Rayong but not in a high-rise on a busy main road full of traffic · it isn't a beachfront resort like the ones at Samet or Mae Ramphueng, and it isn't a glass-tower business hotel purely for people in town for factory work · instead it's a Rayong River hotel set in the old quarter, near Yommarat Road — the city's first street and its historic trading district · the selling point is the calm riverside atmosphere, the green garden, and a "resting in the middle of the city" feeling that's hard to find in downtown Rayong · open since 2008 and renovated in 2023, it's still running today and earns a "very good" score on the booking platforms · real reviews suggest the people who fit best here are couples after a quiet stay with some atmosphere, families who drive to Rayong and want to use the city as a base for beach trips, travelers who like wandering the old quarter and cafés, and people in town for work who don't want to sleep somewhere too bland · the group it may not suit is anyone who wants a swimming pool, because there isn't one, and anyone expecting five-star luxury, because this is a three-star hotel selling charm and a riverside location rather than luxury.

Location and getting around — this is what sets Madina apart from the usual Rayong city hotels · the hotel sits at 41 Rim Nam Road, Tha Pradu, Mueang Rayong, in a spot that runs parallel to the Rayong River and is within walking distance of Yommarat Road, the preserved old quarter · Yommarat Road was conceived by Phra Si Samut Phok (Im Yommarat), Rayong's last governor, as the city's first street, lined with wooden shophouses and buildings over a century old, and it has now been revived as a place to stroll, with cafés, food shops and art studios tucked into the old buildings · nearby there's also a riverside park, Rim Nam Garden, about a 5-minute walk away, perfect for a morning or evening walk · for getting further afield, the hotel's own information notes it's about 5 minutes from government offices, the courthouse, schools and parks, about a 10 min drive to Tesco and the beach, around 15 minutes to Central Plaza Rayong and Passione, and easy to reach Sukhumvit Road and the Map Ta Phut industrial estate · U-Tapao Airport (UTP) is about a 30 min drive away, handy for anyone flying in · one thing to note: the riverside location in the old quarter is on a lane that isn't very wide, so if you're driving yourself, allow a little patience for the approach — but once you arrive there's free private parking.

"I loved that it's a riverside hotel right in town — wake up, open the door to a quiet river view, walk a few minutes to Yommarat Road for food. The staff were excellent, and breakfast was tastier than I'd expect for a hotel this size."

Room types and decor — Madina Hotel Rayong has 72 rooms in all, split across several categories to suit your budget and how much you care about the view · starting with the Standard Room of about 24–32 sqm, mostly set up with two single beds, good for friends or a solo traveler who wants a not-too-large room at a budget price · stepping up to the Standard Room with River View of about 25–32 sqm adds the river view, which many people happily pay more for since it's the main draw here · the Superior Room of about 32 sqm usually has a single queen bed, good for couples · and the room many people recommend is the Deluxe Room with River View of about 32 sqm, a queen bed with a full river view · the decor is contemporary with a touch of Thai feel, in line with the hotel's lifestyle concept, in warm, easy-on-the-eyes tones · every room has a private balcony, work desk, air-con, TV, private bathroom and free Wi-Fi · many reviews agree that the rooms are clean, a good size, and the beds comfortable, especially given the fairly low starting price · one thing worth knowing that guests mention: the building has been open since 2008, so some corners feel their age even after the 2023 renovation, and water pressure in some bathrooms may not be as strong as a newer hotel · anyone who cares about the river view should request a River View room when booking, since the garden-view and city-view rooms have a noticeably different feel.

Facilities and the riverside space — let's be straight up front: Madina Hotel Rayong has no swimming pool, which is worth knowing before you book if you're coming to swim at the hotel · what the hotel leans on instead is the riverside atmosphere and green space · a favorite spot is the garden and lawn along the Rayong River, set up as an area to sit, take photos, and hold riverside events, with a calm atmosphere that's ideal for a morning or evening coffee · for fitness there's a gym and a yoga space for anyone wanting a light workout · other shared services include a 24-hour reception, luggage storage, room service, and meeting and function rooms for small to mid-size events or seminars · importantly for anyone driving themselves, there's free private parking, an advantage for a hotel with land in the old quarter, plus free Wi-Fi in the common areas · overall the facilities here are about right for a three-star riverside hotel — not loaded with the toys of a big resort, but enough for a relaxing stay and for using the city as a base for day trips.

Food and café — food is where Madina earns more praise than you'd expect for a hotel this size · the main restaurant is Kesara Restaurant, open from morning to evening (about 6:00 AM–7:00 PM), serving both a breakfast buffet and à la carte · interestingly, it's also open to non-guests for breakfast, which suggests the hotel is fairly confident in the kitchen · several real reviews agree that breakfast is tasty and varied, with both Thai and standard international dishes, all fresh · another thing that gives the place charm is Two Hundreds Coffee, a specialty coffee café inside the hotel open about 8:00 AM–4:00 PM, good for a mid-morning riverside coffee or a break during the day · for other meals, the hotel's location helps a lot, since a short walk takes you to Yommarat Road with its food shops, cafés and long-running dessert shops of old Rayong, and Rayong is also known for fresh seafood and local products like fish sauce and shrimp paste · so many people eat breakfast at the hotel and head out for good food elsewhere at lunch and dinner, which fits the style of using the hotel as a base for exploring the city.

Service — service is a strength that comes up again and again in Madina's real reviews · the words you see often are that the staff are good, friendly, attentive and happy to help, from check-in through to recommending places to visit and eat in town · for a not-too-large 72-room hotel, the team can look after guests fairly thoroughly and with a personal touch, which is a charm hotels at this level can do well · the reception is open 24 hours, with luggage storage and room service, handy for anyone arriving late or leaving early · to be fair, some reviews note that certain amenities are basic and that some items may carry an extra charge, along with parts of the older building that need upkeep with age · but overall, the warmth and care of the team are what leave many guests impressed and speaking positively about the place.

What real reviews say (the good and the not-so-good) — pulled together from Trip.com, Agoda, Booking.com and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · on the praise side: a quiet, atmospheric in-town riverside location, walkable to the Yommarat Road old town and the riverside park, tasty and varied breakfast, good and friendly staff, clean and well-sized rooms, and free parking that's handy for self-drivers · the low starting price relative to what you get is another thing many people are happy with · on the watch-out side: what comes up is the building, open since 2008, so some corners feel their age even after the 2023 renovation; water pressure in some bathrooms isn't very strong; some amenities are basic and a few items carry an extra charge; and importantly, there's no swimming pool, which may not suit anyone set on swimming at the hotel · most of these criticisms are things you can accept if you set expectations from the start, because this is a three-star hotel selling the charm of a riverside location and its service, not luxury or a full set of amenities.

"Great value for the price — clean room, lovely staff, good breakfast · the only knocks are no pool and the building starting to show its age, but the riverside atmosphere makes up for it all. Next time I'm in Rayong I'll stay here again."

Price and value — Madina Hotel Rayong's starting price is around THB 700–900/night for a Standard room in normal periods, rising to about THB 1,000–1,500/night for a River View or Deluxe room on weekends and in high season · compared with other Rayong city hotels, Madina sits in the group of accessible prices but more atmosphere than the price suggests · against big city hotels like Golden City Rayong or Kameo, which focus on lots of rooms, large meeting rooms and plenty of parking, Madina is smaller and has no pool, but wins on the charm of its riverside location and proximity to the old quarter · against budget hotels like Hop Inn or general budget hotels, Madina offers more atmosphere and green space for a similar price · in short, if you value waking up to a river view, strolling the old quarter, and getting a good breakfast for a budget of just over a thousand baht, this place is good value — but if you must have a pool or want a brand-new building, you may need to look at pricier options.

Good to know before you book — a few things make the stay smoother · one, if you value the river view, request a River View room when booking, since garden-view or city-view rooms have a different feel · two, know in advance that the hotel has no swimming pool — if this trip needs swimming, consider a beachfront resort instead · three, check-in is 2:00 PM–11:00 PM and check-out before 12:00 PM; if you arrive early you can store your luggage first · four, self-drivers can relax about the free parking, but allow a little patience for the approach along the not-very-wide lane in the old quarter · five, plan to stroll Yommarat Road and the riverside park in the morning or evening when it's cooler, and allow time to head out to the beach and malls about 10–15 min drive away · six, if newness of the room matters to you, ask for a room in the part renovated in 2023, and set expectations mainly around value and atmosphere.

The bottom line — from all the real reviews, Madina Hotel Rayong is the best fit for people who want to stay in central Rayong in a quiet riverside setting, near the Yommarat Road old town, on an accessible budget · the charm of the riverside location, the green garden, breakfast that's better than the price, an in-house coffee shop, warm service and free parking make it a lovely choice for a city trip and a base for beach outings · but you have to accept there's no pool, that it's a building open since 2008 with some details that show their age, and that the facilities are at the basic level of a three-star hotel · if you're after luxury, a pool, or a full beachfront resort, this may not be the answer and you should consider the Mae Ramphueng beach side or Koh Samet instead · but for anyone who wants to experience Rayong from its riverside old-town angle, with attentive service at a good-value price — Madina is a hotel that meets that need with real charm.

faq.q: Where is Madina Hotel Rayong, and what can you walk to?
faq.a: The hotel is at 41 Rim Nam Road, Tha Pradu, Mueang Rayong, on the Rayong River in the old quarter · it's within walking distance of Yommarat Road, the historic trading district of century-old wooden shophouses, and Rim Nam Garden riverside park (about 0.4 km) · it's about a 10 min drive to the beach and Tesco, ~15 min to Central and Passione malls, and ~30 min to U-Tapao Airport.

faq.q: Does Madina Hotel Rayong have a swimming pool?
faq.a: There's no swimming pool · the hotel focuses on the riverside atmosphere, green garden, and a gym and yoga space instead · if this trip is about swimming, we'd suggest a resort on the Mae Ramphueng beach side or nearby Koh Samet.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Madina Hotel Rayong, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 700/night for a Standard room in normal periods · there are Standard, Standard River View, Superior and Deluxe River View rooms of about 24–32 sqm · river-view rooms and weekends cost more, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Madina Hotel Rayong best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples, families and travelers who want to stay in central Rayong in a quiet riverside setting, near the Yommarat Road old town, on an accessible budget · it works well as a base for beach trips and for strolling the old quarter · if you're after a pool or a full beachfront resort, the beach side may suit you better.

faq.q: What are breakfast and the café like at Madina?
faq.a: The main restaurant is Kesara Restaurant, serving a breakfast buffet and à la carte, and many real reviews praise it for being tasty and varied · there's also the Two Hundreds Coffee café in the hotel for a riverside coffee, and a short walk takes you to the long-running food shops on Yommarat Road.

faq.q: Is parking easy at Madina Hotel Rayong if you drive yourself?
faq.a: The hotel has free private parking, an advantage for self-drivers · one thing to know is that it's in the riverside old quarter where the lane isn't very wide, so allow a little patience for the approach — but once you reach the hotel there's space to park.
